title: Uniform provisions concerning the approval of Vehicle Alarm Systems (VAS) and of vehicles with regard to their alarm systems (AS)
scope_summary: Part I approves Vehicle Alarm Systems (VAS) as components intended to be permanently fitted to vehicles of any category, and Part II approves vehicles of category M1 and N1 (max. mass not more than 2 t) with regard to their alarm system(s). Approval of other vehicle categories is optional at the manufacturer's request; only 12 V electrical systems are considered, and radio transmission frequencies are excluded.
scope_quote: 1.1 Approval of Vehicle Alarm Systems (VAS) which are intended to be permanently fitted to vehicles of any category. 1.2 Approval of vehicles of category M1 and those of category N1 with a maximum mass of not more than 2 tonnes, with regard to their alarm system(s). 1.3 At the request of the manufacturer, Contracting Parties may grant approvals to vehicles of other categories with regard to their alarm system(s). 1.4 This UN Regulation does not apply to radio transmission frequencies, whether or not related to the protection of vehicles against unauthorized use.

relation_to_other_regulations: Vehicle categories as defined in the Consolidated Resolution on the Construction of Vehicles (R.E.3), ECE/TRANS/WP.29/78/Rev.6.
Distinguishing country numbers for approval mark per Annex 3 to R.E.3.
Approval mark may be combined with marks under other UN Regulations (para 4.5).
Excludes radio transmission frequencies (para 1.4), which are regulated elsewhere.
Annex 7 EMC immunity/emission tests refer to external technical prescriptions (EMC test standards); Annex 9 addresses cyber-attack resilience of digital keys.
Content historically derives from the alarm-system provisions of UN R97/R116 (not stated in the excerpt).

defined_terms.definition: A device subject to the requirements of this Regulation, intended to be part of a vehicle, which may be type-approved independently of a vehicle where expressly provided.
A device subject to this Regulation, intended to be part of a vehicle, which may be type-approved separately but only in relation to one or more specified vehicle types.
A system intended for installation on vehicle type(s), designed to indicate intrusion into or interference with the vehicle, possibly providing additional protection against unauthorized use.
A device which senses a change which could be caused by intrusion into or interference with a vehicle.
A device indicating that intrusion into or interference has occurred.
Equipment necessary for the setting, unsetting and testing of a VAS and for sending an alarm condition to warning devices.
The state of a VAS in which an alarm condition can be transmitted to warning devices.
The state of a VAS in which an alarm condition cannot be transmitted to warning devices.
Any mechanical and/or electronic solution designed and constructed to provide a method of operating a locking system designed to be operated by it.
Systems not differing significantly in trade name or mark, kind of sensor, kind of warning device and kind of control equipment.
A device intended to prevent the vehicle being driven away powered by its own engine.
A device enabling a person to use an alarm installed on the vehicle to summon assistance in an emergency.

applicability_hints: Aftermarket alarm kits permanently fitted to vehicles of any category fall under Part I as a VAS component.
Factory-fitted alarm systems on M1 and N1 (≤ 2 t) vehicles fall under Part II vehicle approval.
Sensors such as ultrasonic/volumetric intrusion, tilt, door/bonnet/boot contact sensors are VAS sensors.
Sirens, horns and hazard/direction-indicator lamps used to signal an alarm are warning devices; lamps used in the optical warning are addressed in section 7.

Remote key fobs, transponder keys, smartphone/digital keys used to set/unset the alarm are control equipment/keys; digital keys trigger Annex 9 (including cyber security), but radio frequencies themselves are out of scope.
External key switches must meet Annex 6 (cylinder protrusion, drill obstruction, ≥1000 key permutations).
Status-display LEDs/telltales indicating set/unset state are covered by 6.9/11.9.
Panic alarm buttons are optional functions under 6.11/11.11.
Electronic alarm control units must meet EMC immunity and emission tests of Annex 7.
Only 12 V electrical systems are considered.
